title: Hand-Rolled Orecchiette with Broccoli, Garlic and Chilli
summary: Hand-shaped semolina orecchiette cooked with broccoli and tossed in a garlicky, chilli-spiked olive oil sauce.
equipment: table knife with a rounded tip
large frying pan or sauté pan (30 cm)

ingredients.item: fine semolina (semola rimacinata), plus extra for dusting
broccoli rabe (cime di rapa) or tenderstem broccoli, trimmed and cut into 3 cm pieces
fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 5.25 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: pecorino-style hard cheese (microbial rennet), finely grated

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Put the semolina in a bowl, make a well in the centre, and pour in the water. Stir with your fingertips until it clumps together, adding the extra 1-2 tablespoons of water only if dry flour remains at the bottom.

steps.title: Knead until smooth
steps.text: Knead the dough on a clean worktop for 8-10 minutes, until it turns smooth and firm and no longer looks gritty. Semolina takes a while to hydrate fully, so the kneading time is what brings it together rather than extra water.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Wrap the dough and leave it to rest for 30 minutes before shaping.

steps.title: Shape the orecchiette
steps.text: Cut the dough into 6 pieces, keeping the rest covered, and roll one piece at a time into a 1.5 cm rope on the bare worktop, then cut it into 1 cm pieces. Put the rounded tip of a table knife on the far edge of a piece and drag it towards you with firm pressure, so the dough curls into a rough little shell, then flip it over your thumb to form a cupped, ear-shaped piece with a rough outer surface - that texture is what catches the sauce later. For cavatelli, drag with two fingers instead and leave the dough curled rather than flipping it.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli and pasta
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to the boil with the 32 g salt. Add the broccoli and cook for 2 minutes, then add the orecchiette and cook both together for 4-5 minutes more, until the pasta is tender with a firm centre and the broccoli is soft. Reserve 240 ml of the cooking water before draining.

steps.title: Warm the garlic and chilli
steps.text: While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil, garlic and chilli flakes in a large frying pan over medium-low heat for 2-3 minutes, until the garlic turns pale gold.

steps.title: Toss together
steps.text: Lift the pasta and broccoli into the pan with 80 ml of the reserved water, and toss over medium-high heat for 1-2 minutes, pressing down on some of the broccoli so it breaks up and melts into the oil. This is what turns the broccoli into a rough, green, oily coating rather than separate florets.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide between bowls and finish with the grated pecorino-style cheese.

tips: Keep the worktop bare when shaping the pasta - flour stops the knife tip gripping the dough enough to curl it properly.
Cook the broccoli and pasta together in the same pot rather than separately; the starchy water helps the sauce come together later.
Press some of the broccoli into the sauce as you toss so it breaks down slightly - leaving every piece whole makes for a drier, less cohesive dish.
If the garlic browns before the pasta is ready, take the pan off the heat briefly; burnt garlic turns bitter very quickly.

The same dough makes the other shapes in the photo: roll small pieces under your palm into thin twists for trofie, or roll thick ropes about 5 mm wide and 20 cm long for pici. Pici need 6-8 minutes in the pot, trofie about 5.
storage: Shaped, uncooked orecchiette can be frozen on a tray then bagged for up to 2 months and cooked straight from frozen, adding a minute or two to the time. The finished dish is best eaten fresh, but leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat well in a pan with a splash of water until piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
